chunks: The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Istarabadi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to us from their fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from the Commander of the Faithful (God’s blessings upon him). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:
God, Blessed and Exalted, said: I have divided the Opening of the Book between Me and My servant. Half of it is for Me and half of it is for My servant, and for My servant is whatever he asks.

When the servant says: “In the name of God, the Beneficent, the Merciful,” God, exalted is His Majesty, says: “My servant has begun with My name, and it is My duty to fulfill his affairs and to bless him in his conditions.” When he says: “All praise belongs to God, the Lord of the Worlds,” God, exalted is His Majesty, says: “My servant has praised Me and he knows that the blessings he has are from Me, and that the calamities that were deflected from him were due to My grace. I testify to you that I will add to the blessings of this world for him the blessings of the Hereafter, and I will deflect from him the calamities of the Hereafter just as I deflected from him the calamities of this world.”

When he says: “The Beneficent, the Merciful,” God says: “He has testified for Me that I am the Beneficent, the Merciful. I testify to you that I will surely increase his portion of My mercy and grant him generously his share of My bestowal.” When he says: “Master of the Day of Judgment,” God says: “I testify to you: just as he has acknowledged that I am the Master of the Day of Judgment, I will ease his reckoning, accept his good deeds, and overlook his sins.” When he says: “You alone we worship,” God says: “My servant has spoken the truth — he worships Me alone. I will reward him for his worship with a reward envied by all who opposed him.” When he says: “And from You alone we seek help,” God says: “He seeks help in Me and takes refuge in Me. I will help him in his affairs, assist him in his hardships, and take him by his hand in his calamities.”

When he says: “Guide us to the Straight Path” to the end of the surah, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: “This is for My servant, and for My servant is whatever he asks. I have answered My servant, I have given him what he hoped for, and I have secured him from that which he fears.”

key_terms.أشهدكم: Ushidukum: I testify to you / I call you to witness — God addressing the angels
key_terms.تبارك وتعالى: Tabarak wa Ta’ala: Blessed and Exalted — a divine honorific
key_terms.فاتحة الكتاب: Fatihat al-Kitab: The Opening of the Book, i.e. Surah al-Fatiha, the first chapter of the Quran recited in every prayer
key_terms.نوائبه: Nawa’ibuhu: his calamities, afflictions, or moments of distress

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of Surah al-Fatiha according to a Hadith Qudsi?
ai.summary: In this Hadith Qudsi narrated through the chain of Imams back to Imam Ali (AS) and the Prophet (SAWW), God reveals the spiritual significance of Surah al-Fatiha as a dialogue between Himself and His worshipping servant. Each verse of the Fatiha elicits a divine promise: beginning with God’s name earns the completion of affairs; praising God earns blessings of both worlds; acknowledging His mercy earns increased mercy; recognizing His sovereignty eases the Day of Judgment; declaring exclusive worship earns unmatched reward; seeking His help guarantees divine assistance; and asking for guidance brings acceptance of all prayers. This hadith was taught in the context of encouraging sincere engagement with prayer, revealing that the daily recitation of al-Fatiha is not mere ritual but an intimate exchange with the Creator.
